problem.text: Comparison plots previously selected colors only from format-name substrings, leaving unmatched labels black and displaying the entire label.

reasoning.text: The change separates display text from color selection: bracketed color names override format matching, while the visible label stops at the first opening bracket.

impact.text: Color overrides also change connecting-line membership: existing plotting code groups points by color and excludes black points from lines. Evaluation scores and printed result labels are unchanged.

limitations: The check transcribed string-selection logic using standard-library Python; it did not execute the repository plotting function, Matplotlib rendering, or model evaluation.

claims.text: plot.get_color first searches for exact bracketed palette values: [green], [purple], [olive], [brown], [red], [blue], and [black]. It then falls back to format-name matching and finally black. This supports explicit overrides without adding a separate result field.
The new **** mapping supplies another black fallback marker, but does not outrank earlier format matches. Multiple bracketed colors are resolved in palette iteration order, not their textual order.

Displayed annotations strip surrounding whitespace from the portion before the first '[' and retain the newline plus perplexity formatted to three decimal places. Truncation applies even to unrecognized bracket content; color selection still receives the original full label.

A scalar transcription selected red for 'EXL3 demo [red]', black for 'EXL3 demo [black]', purple for 'EXL3 ****', and green for 'custom [red] [green]'. It also confirmed that 'demo [unknown] suffix' displays only 'demo' before the score.

annotation.summary: Adds bracketed palette-color overrides and hides bracket suffixes in comparison-plot labels; chosen colors also control existing connecting-line groups.
